title: The Pythagorean Theorem
learning_objective: In a right triangle, the square built on the hypotenuse has exactly the same area as the squares on the two legs combined.
running_example: The 3-4-5 right triangle: legs a = 3 and b = 4, hypotenuse c = 5, whose squares hold 9, 16 and 25 unit cells.

scenes.caption: A right triangle has two legs, a = 3 and b = 4, and a longest side, the hypotenuse c = 5.
scenes.visual_description: A 3-4-5 right triangle on the left with its legs colored blue (a) and purple (b), the hypotenuse cyan (c), and a small right-angle mark. On the right, three chips list a = 3, b = 4 and c = 5 with the words leg, leg and hypotenuse.
animation_instructions: Draw the three sides of the triangle one after another (1.5 s).
Fade in the faint fill and the right-angle mark (0.8 s).
Write the side labels a = 3, b = 4, c = 5 next to their sides (1.2 s).
Bring in the three chips on the right, then pulse the hypotenuse and hold (2.5 s).
scenes.transition: The triangle and the chips stay; the side labels make way for squares on each side.

scenes.caption: Build a square on each side. Counting unit cells gives areas 3² = 9, 4² = 16 and 5² = 25.
scenes.visual_description: A square grows outward from each side, divided into unit cells: 3 by 3 blue cells on a, 4 by 4 purple cells on b, and a tilted 5 by 5 cyan grid on c, with 9, 16 and 25 written in their centers. The chips update to a² = 9, b² = 16 and c² = 25.
animation_instructions: Fade out the side labels and draw the three square outlines (1 s).
Fill the a-square cell by cell, then the b-square, then the c-square (4.2 s).
Write 9, 16 and 25 inside the squares and update the chips to the areas, then hold (2.6 s).
scenes.transition: Everything stays; the big square's own cells empty out so the small cells can move in.

scenes.concept: Small squares fill the big one
scenes.caption: Move the 9 blue and 16 purple cells into the big square: they fill it exactly, so 9 + 16 = 25.
scenes.visual_description: The cyan cells of the hypotenuse square turn into empty outlines. Copies of the 3 by 3 blue block slide and rotate into one corner of it, and the 16 purple cells fly into the L-shaped region that remains, filling every cell. On the right, 9 + 16 = 25 appears in matching colors.
animation_instructions: Empty the cyan cells of the big square, leaving outlines (0.7 s).
Slide a copy of the blue 3 by 3 block into the corner of the big square (1.6 s).
Fly the 16 purple cells into the remaining L-shaped cells one after another (2.4 s).
Write 9 + 16 = 25 on the right, pulse the filled square and hold (3 s).
scenes.transition: The figure stays; the chips and the sum give way to the general formula.

scenes.caption: This works for every right triangle: the two leg squares together equal the hypotenuse square.
scenes.visual_description: The filled figure stays on the left. On the right the formula a² + b² = c² appears large, colored blue, purple and cyan, with 3² + 4² = 5² beneath it and a note that it holds for every right triangle.
animation_instructions: Clear the chips and the sum from the right side (0.6 s).
Write a² + b² = c² in matching colors, then 3² + 4² = 5² beneath it (2.4 s).
Trace a highlight around the formula, add the note, and hold the final frame (3.5 s).
scenes.transition: The video ends holding the figure and the formula.
